notes: REJECTED 2026-11-13 (Andrew, 2026-11-13: "those clocks are too dark / hard to read. the first one is terrible and I get a headache trying to make out numbers."): a black face with thin rose-gold numerals is too dark to read at a glance; F-70 revised: legibility first. CANDIDATE 2026-11-13, the dining room's clock, the pick (Andrew, 2026-11-13: "I need help getting clocks for the living room and dining or both. be mindful of entry way, where sofa, dining tables are etc so clock positions are optimal. At least one must be analog."). Placement: the dining room's right wall (119 in, derived), centered on the LISABO's long axis as staged in dining-room a (77.6 in from the open top side), its center 58 in off the floor. Why there: the table's end wall, so all four chairs read it with the same turn at about 5 ft; from the kitchen it is square across the dining room (16 ft, 5 degrees); from the top of the stairs 23 ft at 21 degrees, if the dining room sits under the living room's right end (its offset is not measured); and the bottom wall stays for the buffet and canvas staged there. Read 2026-11-13: $49.99, 4.4 stars (6,930), 18 Inch, B_black, 2.7 lb, "black MDF clock face and rose gold Arabic numbers, khaki wooden hour and minute hands, no second hand, no frames and no glass" (F-21), "Silent non-ticking quartz sweep movement". Color (F-68): the room's dark note at eye level on the cream wall, which the ash LISABO doesn't give the white marble (F-68 (10)); the warm metal numerals sit with the brass door knobs; in one sightline with the living room's walnut-and-black clock, a sibling and not a twin (F-68 (2)): both black, round, with Arabic numerals; wood hands here, a wood center there; 18 in to its 24 in. Whether this wall has a doorway is not recorded (rooms.json): if it has, keep the clock on solid wall nearest the table's axis. rooms: the brief.
